our_argument_summary: Stellar aberration is achromatic; refraction is chromatic. Kramers-Kronig forbids any causal physical medium with n>1 from being achromatic. VLBI (~GHz) and optical/Gaia (~500 THz) measure the same aberration constant across roughly six orders of magnitude in frequency, empirically falsifying any refractive mechanism. Annual periodicity rules out any static refractive index. Dome alpha = 2.56e-8 has no derivation from dome geometry. detail_extra (EXP-286) preempts the alpha-as-fitted-coefficient retreat by granting the KK technical concession and showing three independent demands survive; preempts the annual-aether-circulation escape via heliocentric kinematics equivalence + dome static-disc ontology + WIN-017 Gaia handcuff. Verdict: Refuted by Data with Part 3.1b post-hoc tag. WIN-016 has been substantively closed since c5 and textually clean since c6. Spot-check reconfirms substantive closure and flags one downstream cross-WIN consistency finding (ISS-1841 closure was optimistic — 4 of the 7 boilerplate WINs still ship the exact text WIN-016 correctly rejected).

holes_found.description: detail_evidence and detail_extra both assert the aberration measurements span 'six orders of magnitude in frequency' ('10^6× in frequency'). The claim is defensible for the broadest VLBI+optical span (LOFAR ~100 MHz to Gaia optical ~500 THz gives ~5e6× ≈ 6.7 orders), but standard-cm VLBI (~1-30 GHz) to Gaia (~500 THz) is only ~5.2-5.7 orders. A picky defender could grep our numbers, find that the specific VLBI installations we link to (ivscc.gsfc.nasa.gov) are cm-band, and argue we've overstated the span. Not false — just loose. Impact is low: the KK argument doesn't depend on the exact number of orders (any measurable achromaticity across a non-trivial frequency span is enough), so tightening from 'six' to 'over five' or 'roughly six' would cost nothing rhetorically and remove the pedantic attack surface. Fresh grep this cycle: 'six orders of magnitude' appears once in detail_evidence; '10⁶× in frequency' appears once in the same paragraph.
holes_found.recommendation: Optional tightening: replace 'six orders of magnitude in frequency' with 'roughly six orders of magnitude in frequency (LOFAR ~100 MHz to Gaia optical ~500 THz)' and 'agreement across 10⁶× in frequency' with 'agreement across ~10⁵–10⁶× in frequency' (or drop the numeric multiplier and rely on the qualitative claim). Below the threshold to elevate this WIN back to priority queue on its own; consider bundling with any other WIN-016 polish if one comes up. If left alone, no substantive damage.

stronger_arguments.description: The refractive-plausibility side check (this c7 quantitative verification) yields a nice one-line reinforcement of the reverse-engineering critique: for alpha=2.56e-8 to reproduce 20.5 arcsec via a plain refractive formula theta=(n-1)*tan(zenith), the required zenith angle is 89.985 deg — near-horizon, tan(zenith)~3879. That is, alpha=2.56e-8 is 3-4 orders of magnitude too small to be a plausible (n-1) for any reasonable line-of-sight. This complements the existing derivation critique ('no dome-geometric combination reproduces 2.56e-8') with an independent physical-plausibility angle: even if the dome offered a derivation, the numerical value falls outside the realistic range for a refractive coefficient. Optional addition to detail_extra paragraph 1 or as a new bullet in the three-demand argument. Not a hole; a possible sharpening.
